lede: A RealNVP posterior on full MNIST digits reconstructs softly and samples every class. Train and test match.
points: VAE · normalizing flow in the latent space
title: f-VAE
question: Does a RealNVP inside the VAE latent space improve reconstruction and likelihood on digits?
process: The encoder proposes a Gaussian, four coupling layers warp it, and the decoder reads the flowed code. KL is a Monte Carlo estimate of that RealNVP posterior against N(0, I). ELBO is the negative of the training objective. Bits per dimension use the Gaussian decoder that matches the squared error. Reconstruction grids decode the flowed posterior mean. The sample grid decodes draws from N(0, I), not an inverse through the flow: the flow is inside the posterior. The run is digits only, latent 32, hidden 256, 4 flows, full split of 60,000 / 10,000. There is no Fashion f-VAE and no Optuna plot.

opening.summary: Test MSE is 0.0554 and test ELBO is −69.35, essentially the same as train. Prior samples are soft digits from many classes. The flow’s test log-det is −12.87, so it is changing volume rather than sitting at the identity.
opening.hover: Hover a row for the number behind that sentence.

marks.label: Reconstruction
marks.summary: Test MSE 0.0554 and MAE 0.0920. Train is 0.0555 and 0.0923. The flowed posterior mean keeps the digit and softens the stroke. This is a full 60,000-image run at latent 32, so it is not the same setup as the latent-8 slice VAE.

marks.label: Likelihood
marks.summary: Test ELBO −69.35 and BPD 0.953, against train ELBO −69.40 and BPD 0.953. The bound held on the 10,000 test images. A Gaussian decoder can report a decent BPD while the pictures stay soft, because the likelihood averages over stroke positions.

marks.label: Flow
marks.summary: Test log-det is −12.87 and train is −12.85. The flow is not an identity at the end of training: it rescales latent volume. KL stays near 19.5 on both splits. The sample picture is still a decode of N(0, I); the inverse flow is used in the posterior, not as the gallery generator.

marks.label: Prior samples
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: The 64 prior samples cover 0–9 and a few ambiguous blobs. They are cleaner than the RealNVP inverse grid and softer than a sharp GAN. The flow fixed the posterior shape. It did not give the decoder a sharper pixel likelihood.

marks.label: Fashion-MNIST
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: The flow-in-latent model was only trained on digits. There is no paired Fashion f-VAE to set next to the slice VAE comparison.

reflection.worked: Reconstruction and the ELBO agree between train and test on the full digits split. Samples from the prior look like digits across classes, and a log-det near −13 shows the couplings are doing work.
reflection.unexpected: The pictures stay soft, and a few samples are blobs. Putting RealNVP in the latent space did not produce the crisp inverse-flow samples the pure flow was missing, because these samples never go through that inverse.
reflection.why: Squared error trains the decoder to average every stroke that could explain a code. The flow can make the posterior a better match to the prior and still leave that average in pixel space. Comparing ELBO with the latent-8 slice VAE would mix latent size, dataset size, and the flow term.
reflection.improve: Train the same f-VAE on Fashion and quote BPD beside the sample grid. If the goal is sharp digits, change the decoder likelihood or add the class-conditional GAN lesson below. More coupling layers will not sharpen a Gaussian decoder by themselves.
